question.text: Per the Investor Charter Annexure, NAV of a Cat III OPEN-ENDED AIF scheme must be disclosed at what minimum frequency?

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9 Annexure 9.1 Section D states: 'Disclosure of NAV of scheme(s) of the Category III Alternative Investment Fund: Close ended fund - quarterly basis; Open ended fund - monthly basis.' Monthly is the minimum for open-ended Cat III disclosure. The Trap: Option A over-discloses. Options C and D are close-ended/Cat I-II territory. Many candidates mix up the 'daily NAV computation' (internal practice) with the 'monthly NAV disclosure' (regulatory floor). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers the same NAV-disclosure table. XIX-D tests Cat I/II 6-monthly / annual-with-75%-consent valuation. XIX-B tests the distributor's obligation to relay NAV to clients. Manager's Pro-Tip: Though regulation is monthly, most Cat III hedge-funds compute NAV DAILY for internal risk / HWM crystallisation and publish weekly to investors — outperforming the regulatory floor is a light-touch differentiator in fundraising.
